title: Joginder Kumar v. State of UP
summary: No arrest can be made merely because it is lawful for the police officer to do so. Arrest is a serious matter affecting personal liberty. The arrestee must be informed of the grounds of arrest. A relative or friend of the arrested person must be informed of the arrest and the place of detention. title: D.K. Basu v. State of West Bengal
summary: Mandatory guidelines for arrest and detention: (1) arresting officer must bear visible identification; (2) arrest memo must be prepared at the time of arrest, attested by a family member or respectable person, and countersigned by the arrested person; (3) grounds of arrest must be communicated; (4) a relative or friend must be informed of the arrest and place of custody; (5) arrested person must be produced before a Magistrate within 24 hours. Violation of these guidelines entitles the victim to compensation as a public-law remedy under Articles 21 and 226.
holding: Mandatory guidelines on arrest procedure to prevent custodial violence; violation is actionable and may ground contempt of court.
